date_note: FinCEN's statement was issued on Tuesday per Türkiye Gazetesi's article of 25 November; resolved to 24 November.
geo_basis: agency headquarters, Washington DC (US Treasury unit)
title: FinCEN says unauthorized access hit a limited part of its systems, Türkiye Gazetesi reports
summary: Türkiye Gazetesi reports that the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), a US Treasury unit, said in a statement on Tuesday it is investigating a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to a limited part of its systems. The article says FinCEN took some systems offline as a precaution and that the scope and source were not disclosed. AITNews, citing a FinCEN alert, adds that FinCEN issued an order extending some reporting deadlines.
plain: A Turkish newspaper reports that FinCEN, a US Treasury unit, says it is investigating unauthorized access to a limited part of its systems and took some systems offline as a precaution.
exec: Per the article, banks file suspicious activity reports with FinCEN online, some services may not be immediately accessible, and the scope and source were not disclosed.
action: General advice: banks with urgent reports should use the help line the article says was not affected; otherwise no action needed.

sources.name: Türkiye Gazetesi: ABD'nin kritik kurumlarına peş peşe siber saldırı!

validation.note: Türkiye Gazetesi and AITNews both relay FinCEN's statement and cite The Verge, so treated as single-source. FinCEN's own alert and order PDF were not read (its news-release page loaded without body text).
